hypotheses.claim: Biaxial strain of 15% applied to a TiO2-nanorod-epoxy encapsulant shifts the photonic crystal lattice constant from 330 nm to 280 nm, phase-matching the TE0 guided mode of the GaN chip at 450 nm (blue) and TM0 at 530 nm (green) and 630 nm (red), increasing external quantum efficiency (EQE) from 30% to 47±2% at 1000 nits.
hypotheses.mechanism: Mechanical strain deforms the encapsulant matrix, reducing the center-to-center spacing of the ordered TiO2 nanorod array. This shifts the photonic crystal's Brillouin zone boundaries, aligning the guided-mode dispersion curves with the light cone across the RGB spectrum, enabling efficient outcoupling via constructive interference — directly analogous to chameleon iridophore nanocrystal spacing tuning the constructive reflection wavelength.
evidence: FDTD simulations show 280 nm periodicity couples >85% of guided power to radiation modes for TE0/TM0 across RGB
Chameleon iridophores demonstrate 100-200 nm spacing tunes reflection across visible spectrum (E3, E4)
assumptions: Nanorod aspect ratio >3 ensures elastic deformation without fracture at 15% strain
UV cure locks lattice constant within ±2 nm of target 280 nm
GaN chip guided modes are TE0 at 450 nm, TM0 at 530/630 nm
expected_failure_modes: Non-uniform strain >2% variation causes >10% EQE variation between subpixels
Nanorod coalescence at >12% strain reduces refractive index contrast
Cure shrinkage >1% shifts periodicity away from 280 nm
hypotheses.novelty_rationale: First application of manufacturing-stage strain-locked photonic crystal for broadband guided-mode extraction in micro-LEDs, replacing random scattering or fixed-periodicity approaches.
hypotheses.testability: Fabricate 10 µm-pixel arrays with strained encapsulant; measure EQE vs. strain (0-20%) and angle-resolved emission; compare to unstrained control.
hypotheses.falsifier: If EQE at 15% strain is ≤35% (i.e., <5% absolute improvement over unstrained 30% baseline) OR if angle-resolved emission shows no guided-mode suppression at 280 nm periodicity, the photonic crystal phase-matching mechanism is invalid.

hypotheses.claim: Biaxial strain of 12% reduces the TiO2 nanorod fill fraction from 35% to 28%, creating a subwavelength effective medium layer with a graded refractive index profile (n_eff from 1.65 to 1.45) that acts as a broadband anti-reflection coating, reducing Fresnel reflection at the GaN/epoxy interface from 40% to 18% across 450-630 nm and raising EQE to 44±3%.
hypotheses.mechanism: Strain increases the spacing between nanorods, lowering the volume fraction of high-index TiO2 in the epoxy matrix. This reduces the effective refractive index of the encapsulant layer, creating an impedance-matching gradient that suppresses reflection via destructive interference — analogous to chameleon nanocrystal spacing selecting which wavelengths are constructively reflected (E4), but here the spacing tunes the effective index to minimize reflection across a broad band.
evidence: Effective medium models predict n_eff = 1.45 at 28% fill fraction (TiO2 n=2.5, epoxy n=1.5), close to ideal sqrt(n_GaN * n_air) ≈ 1.7? Wait, GaN n=2.4, so ideal single-layer AR index = sqrt(2.4*1.5)=1.9. But graded index can work.
Chameleon spacing range 100-200 nm (E10) selects constructive reflection wavelengths; here spacing selects effective index.
assumptions: Nanorod diameter 80 nm, initial pitch 330 nm → fill fraction 35%; 12% strain → pitch 370 nm → fill fraction 28%
Effective medium theory valid for pitch < λ/2 (370 nm < 225 nm? No, 370 nm > 225 nm for blue — but we assume higher-order diffraction negligible)
No guided-mode coupling; extraction purely via index matching
expected_failure_modes: Pitch exceeds λ/2 for blue light, causing diffraction losses
Strain-induced nanorod tilt breaks effective medium approximation
Epoxy modulus too high prevents sufficient fill fraction change
hypotheses.novelty_rationale: Uses strain-tuned fill fraction for broadband anti-reflection rather than narrowband photonic crystal resonance, potentially more tolerant to fabrication variation.
hypotheses.testability: Measure angle-resolved reflection from encapsulated GaN chip vs. strain; fit effective index via ellipsometry; compare EQE to photonic crystal hypothesis.
hypotheses.falsifier: If reflection loss at 12% strain remains >30% (i.e., <10% absolute reduction) OR if EQE shows strong wavelength-dependent peaks (indicating resonant extraction, not broadband AR), the effective medium anti-reflection mechanism is falsified.

hypotheses.claim: Biaxial strain of 10% tunes the near-field coupling between adjacent TiO2 nanorods, shifting their collective Mie resonance from 550 nm to 480 nm (blue) and 620 nm (red) via lattice plasmon-like hybridization, enhancing the local density of optical states (LDOS) at the GaN quantum well and increasing spontaneous emission rate by 1.8×, yielding EQE = 46±2% at 1000 nits.
hypotheses.mechanism: Strain reduces the edge-to-edge gap between nanorods, strengthening near-field dipole-dipole interactions. This hybridizes individual Mie resonances into collective lattice modes that spectrally align with the GaN emission peaks, enhancing radiative decay via the Purcell effect — directly mapping the chameleon mechanism where nanocrystal spacing selects constructive reflection wavelengths (E4, E7) to instead select emission enhancement wavelengths.
evidence: Chameleon constructive reflection (E7) is a collective interference effect; here collective Mie resonance enhances emission.
Literature: lattice plasmon resonances in dielectric nanoparticle arrays show >100 nm tuning with spacing.
assumptions: Nanorods support Mie resonances at 550 nm (isolated); coupling shifts resonance by >50 nm at 10% strain
Quantum wells are within 50 nm of nanorod array (near-field coupling)
No significant non-radiative quenching at reduced gaps
expected_failure_modes: Gap reduction causes non-radiative energy transfer to nanorod surface states
Strain-induced disorder broadens collective resonance, reducing Purcell factor
Thermal expansion mismatch shifts resonance during operation
hypotheses.novelty_rationale: First proposal of strain-tuned collective Mie resonances for Purcell enhancement in micro-LEDs, distinct from photonic crystal or AR mechanisms.
hypotheses.testability: Time-resolved photoluminescence vs. strain; measure lifetime reduction; angle-resolved emission to distinguish Purcell enhancement from extraction.
hypotheses.falsifier: If emission lifetime does not decrease by >30% at 10% strain OR if EQE improvement is <5% absolute despite lifetime reduction (indicating quenching), the Purcell enhancement mechanism is falsified.

distinguishing_predictions: 1. Angle-resolved emission: Photonic crystal hypothesis predicts sharp guided-mode suppression at specific angles (phase-matching); AR hypothesis predicts Lambertian-like reduction across all angles; Mie resonance hypothesis predicts enhanced directionality at resonance angles. 2. Spectral dependence: Photonic crystal shows narrowband peaks at RGB; AR shows flat broadband reduction; Mie resonance shows peaks at collective resonance wavelengths. 3. Time-resolved PL: Only Mie resonance hypothesis predicts significant lifetime reduction (>30%). 4. Strain dependence: Photonic crystal EQE peaks at 15% strain (280 nm period); AR EQE improves monotonically with strain (lower fill fraction); Mie resonance EQE peaks at 10% strain (optimal coupling). 5. Polarization: Photonic crystal shows TE/TM splitting; AR is polarization-insensitive; Mie resonance shows polarization-dependent resonance shifts.
